purpose: Prepare synthetic observable fixtures for mobile reuse of the shared sync engine and foreground recovery while all implementation and behavior remain gated.
dependencyPolicy: Conservative gate: require T24 card dependencies T21/T23 and 03 §11 T24 upstream T16/T18/T19. Also enumerate T21 card upstream T14/T17/T19/T20 plus its 03 §11 additions T15/T16/T18, T23 card upstream T15/T22, and the inspected T20 upstream T06/T15 and T22 upstream T06/T07 (including T23→T22→T06/T07). All 12 listed tasks must be accepted before T24 advances. This is not a claim that full recursive task-manifest closure was computed; deeper closure remains T24-OQ01.

dataBoundary.fixtureData: Synthetic account/workspace/device/entity/op identifiers, Decimal strings, state transitions, receipts/cursors, crash barriers, capability categories, injected counters, and opaque byte sentinels only.
dataBoundary.opaqueWireBytes: Non-secret sentinel bytes are only for exact outbox immutability checks; they are not ciphertext, encryption output, nonce material, known-answer vectors, or crypto evidence.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic caller presents a T21 shared TypeScript engine contract and a mobile repository adapter boundary; no implementation is loaded.
fixtures.action: Plan mobile integration through that shared engine and adapter.
fixtures.assertions: Reuse one revision/CAS, outbox, cursor, and snapshot rule set; mobile supplies platform/storage adapters instead of a second sync engine. Exact exports and adapter API remain OPEN_QUESTION.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic unlocked account has cached records, a pending outbox, and injected offline network state.
fixtures.action: Open the library and inspect cached records and sync status offline.
fixtures.assertions: Cached unlocked records remain readable; pending drafts/outbox remain durable; no infinite spinner or deletion; show last successful sync metadata when available.

fixtures.setup: A synthetic foreground event occurs with a persisted READY outbox row and a still-valid account/workspace/unlock state.
fixtures.action: Resume the shared engine on foreground and inspect the dispatch opportunity.
fixtures.assertions: Foreground recovery may resume the persisted row after scope validation; correctness does not depend on a background promise; preserve opId and wire_bytes.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic OS background wake is delayed, coalesced, or omitted while a READY operation is persisted.
fixtures.action: Compare no-wake state with a later foreground event.
fixtures.assertions: Outbox remains recoverable; no continuous background-sync or delivery-time guarantee; foreground resume is the recovery path.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic iOS app is suspended with persisted queue state; no device or OS API is invoked.
fixtures.action: Plan suspend, relaunch/foreground, and local queue inspection.
fixtures.assertions: Check recovery on foreground only; background scheduling outcome remains best-effort and NOT_RUN; suspension is not delivery evidence.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic Android process is killed with a persisted operation; no device or native process is run.
fixtures.action: Plan later foreground launch and outbox recovery.
fixtures.assertions: A persisted row may resume in foreground with original opId/wire_bytes; process death does not permit dropping or regenerating it; no background guarantee.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic persisted row is SENDING with opId=op-kill-01, a non-secret opaque wire_bytes sentinel, and its digest.
fixtures.action: Inject a plan-only process-kill boundary after SENDING persistence; inspect recovered row.
fixtures.assertions: Recovered state is READY; wire_bytes and digest are byte-for-byte unchanged; do not regenerate identity or protocol bytes. Sentinel is not ciphertext/vector.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic opId=op-01 with immutable wire_bytes committed once; response is lost; receipt has revision='4', seq='90'.
fixtures.action: Retry the same opId and exact same bytes; compare receipt and write counts.
fixtures.assertions: Return original receipt/seq; one version/change/usage event only; do not regenerate an operation after a lost response.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic opId=op-02 already has canonical hash h1; a second request has changed bytes/hash h2.
fixtures.action: Submit changed bytes under the same opId.
fixtures.assertions: Return frozen HTTP 409 IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH; stop that op and do not automatically create a replacement opId.

fixtures.setup: Receipt for a synthetic operation confirms revision='8', seq='120'; a later unsent draft depends on that item.
fixtures.action: Plan local ACK transaction recording receipt/revision/seq, clearing acknowledged row, and advancing only the dependent unsent draft.
fixtures.assertions: Persist receipt, confirmedRevision, committedSeq, outbox clearing, and draft-chain state transactionally; no draft loss or invented baseRevision; success only after commit.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic ACK transaction has a pre-commit crash barrier with prior outbox, draft, view, and counter snapshots.
fixtures.action: Inject failure before commit and inspect recovery state.
fixtures.assertions: Rollback is atomic; prior outbox/draft and original bytes are recoverable; no ACK success or cleared operation is visible before commit.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic saved draft references an attachment whose upload dependency is not ready.
fixtures.action: Stage the planned operation and inspect outbox state.
fixtures.assertions: Use frozen WAIT_DEPENDENCY; do not substitute BLOCKED, fabricate ready attachment, or dispatch early.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic attachment dependency later reports ready; its operation has not yet been sent.
fixtures.action: Plan the transition and inspect the queued request.
fixtures.assertions: Do not dispatch before readiness; after readiness use the same planned op identity/bytes and confirmed attachment reference; provider success is not inferred.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic pull spans multiple pages with fixed upperSeq='120'; another change exists beyond that bound.
fixtures.action: Fetch pages using the same upperSeq and inspect toSeq/hasMore.
fixtures.assertions: Every page reuses upperSeq='120'; toSeq advances only through returned changes; no skipped row; next-page request follows local page/cursor commit.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic page rows and prior cursor='89' are prepared with a local transaction crash barrier.
fixtures.action: Apply page/cursor atomically, interrupt before and after commit, then replay the page.
fixtures.assertions: Before commit neither rows nor cursor advances; after commit both appear together; replay is idempotent; HTTP receipt alone never advances cursor.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic seq='100' response arrives before older in-flight seq='99'; a distinct new current-state probe is available.
fixtures.action: Deliver out of order, then make the current-state probe below its own request-time watermark.
fixtures.assertions: High-water remains max; tolerate old response/old upperSeq; isolate only a newly issued current probe below its sent watermark.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic snapshotId=snap-90, epoch='1', H='90'; priorSeenHighWater='120'; catch-up rows 91..120 exist.
fixtures.action: Plan fixed-H pages, catch-up to 120, validation, atomic namespace/cursor swap, then bootstrap ACK.
fixtures.assertions: All pages use same snapshotId/epoch/H='90'; no swap/ACK before catch-up reaches priorSeenHighWater='120'; swap/cursor publish is atomic and ACK follows.

fixtures.setup: Old namespace has a draft and READY old outbox op with immutable bytes; partial recovery snapshot is canceled or expires.
fixtures.action: Cancel recovery, start a new snapshot, and reconcile receipt state before dispatch.
fixtures.assertions: Keep old namespace/draft/outbox; never blindly replay old op; reconcile receipt/entity/version; do not publish partial recovery.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic unlocked cloud body/preview/index canaries sit behind a repository boundary; worker has staged output.
fixtures.action: Lock cloud and directly request the same item through repository/API boundary.
fixtures.assertions: Cloud body/preview/search is rejected or masked at access boundary; stop worker and ignore late output; UI hiding alone is insufficient; display mapping remains OPEN_QUESTION.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic device is revoked with encrypted cache, pending outbox, and a previously issued download lease.
fixtures.action: Attempt a new API/sync/download lease and inspect local-state messaging.
fixtures.assertions: Refuse new authorized API/download work and stop cloud dispatch; handle cached data by user choice; old signed URL may live until frozen TTL; do not claim downloaded plaintext erased.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic accounts A/B have separate workspace IDs, outboxes, subscription states, and non-secret key-handle labels.
fixtures.action: Switch account A to B and inspect namespace ownership and queued requests.
fixtures.assertions: Never reuse A namespace/outbox/key handle under B; never dispatch A wire with B identity; key handles contain no secret.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic async mutation preparation starts under A/WA/revision='7'; barrier allows switch to B/WB before transaction.
fixtures.action: Release preparation and perform transaction-time scope/account/current-revision recheck.
fixtures.assertions: Recheck scope/account/revision inside transaction; mismatch fails closed with no partial draft/view/outbox/counter write or dispatch under B.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic offline index has 40/100 cached entities through indexedUntilSeq='90'; cloudHighWaterSeq='120'.
fixtures.action: Query locally and inspect QueryPage coverage.
fixtures.assertions: Report indexed count/range and incomplete coverage; allow unlocked cache reads; never present partial index as complete cloud search.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic offline account has locked cloud namespace and independently unlocked local-only vault.
fixtures.action: Attempt cloud read while locked, then local-only read.
fixtures.assertions: Locked cloud content/search remains unavailable; local-only follows its own vault state; offline does not unlock cloud or expose locked cache.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic iOS adapter returns permission_required for a user-initiated import capability while an existing outbox is persisted.
fixtures.action: Deny the synthetic capability and inspect import/sync state.
fixtures.assertions: Do not report imported/synced success or discard existing outbox/draft; surface capability fallback category without inventing OS code or claiming device behavior.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic Android adapter reports unsupported/temporarily_unavailable background-capture capability while READY sync row exists.
fixtures.action: Observe capability state and plan foreground resume.
fixtures.assertions: Do not claim background clipboard capture; show capability degradation; existing READY data remains eligible for foreground recovery; native mapping remains OPEN_QUESTION.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic opId=op-cancel-01 push is canceled after dispatch may have reached server; receipt is unresolved.
fixtures.action: Cancel locally, reconnect, and reconcile operation receipt before another write.
fixtures.assertions: Cancellation does not mean server rollback; retain same opId/bytes/draft; unknown receipt is not proof of non-commit; no automatic replacement op.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic cloud outbox is persisted; server responds 401 AUTH_REQUIRED while cloud remains locked.
fixtures.action: Restore login session without device approval/recovery and inspect unlock/outbox state.
fixtures.assertions: Retain outbox/draft on 401; login alone does not unlock cloud; dispatch waits for authorization/unlock; no operation regeneration.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic push receives 503 STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE and a separate request receives 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After.
fixtures.action: Plan bounded retry scheduling and later foreground wake.
fixtures.assertions: Keep original opId/bytes; obey Retry-After and exponential backoff; retain queue; no false commit or immediate spin; no native mapping assumed.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic outbox counter is at configured outboxHardLimitBytes and one byte beyond; values are injected only.
fixtures.action: Attempt a personal_cloud mutation at the boundary and one crossing it.
fixtures.assertions: Block only the new mutation that crosses the limit; preserve old draft/outbox; no silent scope switch or protected-data eviction; actual mobile charge/display remains OPEN_QUESTION.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic local store reports full/unavailable before commit; prior draft/view/outbox/refcount/pendingBytes values are known.
fixtures.action: Attempt one mutation with pre-commit storage failure.
fixtures.assertions: Rollback all affected records/counters together; show no success; retain prior data/old bytes; injected counters do not prove OS capacity.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic JSON push exceeds syncBatchBytes by one UTF-8 byte and contains valid operations.
fixtures.action: Submit oversized batch and inspect response/write counters.
fixtures.assertions: Return HTTP 413 with limitKey='syncBatchBytes' and zero operation/version/change/receipt writes; do not split or partially write request; UI copy remains OPEN_QUESTION.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic positive cloud write receives HTTP 507 QUOTA_EXCEEDED while cached read and separate delete/export choices exist.
fixtures.action: Inspect blocked mutation and permitted read/delete/export paths.
fixtures.assertions: Block new positive cloud delta; retain local data; read/delete/export remain available; no silent deletion or scope conversion.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic stale baseRevision='7'; remote currentRevision='8', currentHeadVersionId=ver-remote-8, currentSeq='120'; local draft is pending.
fixtures.action: Submit stale update and inspect terminal conflict response.
fixtures.assertions: Return HTTP 409 REVISION_CONFLICT with currentRevision/currentHeadVersionId/currentSeq; retain local draft and remote head; no device-clock overwrite or automatic conflict copy.

fixtures.setup: Plan-only alias T24-SHARED-SYNC-01 represents same synthetic workspace/entity/op IDs, epoch/baseRevision/Decimal fields, receipt, cursor, and opaque byte sentinel for desktop/Web/mobile.
fixtures.action: Compare planned adapter projections against the canonical alias; create or modify no shared fixture file.
fixtures.assertions: Adapters are required to preserve canonical IDs, Decimal strings, bytes, receipt/seq, and cursor semantics; this is not observed parity; shared fixture path/owner is OPEN_QUESTION and no crypto result is implied.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic Decimal strings include values above 2^53, signed bigint max='9223372036854775807', and overflow='9223372036854775808'.
fixtures.action: Plan serialization, local persistence, recovery, and cross-adapter projection.
fixtures.assertions: Preserve Decimal strings without Number conversion; max remains exact; overflow returns COUNTER_EXHAUSTED and never wraps; no cryptographic vector is generated.

fixtures.setup: Synthetic-only lifecycle. IDs are fixed, lower-case UUIDv4-format fixture literals and revision values are Decimal strings; these literals do not test CSPRNG/random-source behavior. Desktop creates SavedItem entity id=8f14e45f-ea62-4f9f-8c4e-55c8aabb0001 at content revision "1"; Collection entity id=3c15e2ab-f3c6-4a90-9c72-67e1a0e90002 exists, with no relation yet. Phone caches the unlocked SavedItem offline. Coverage sentinel indexedUntilSeq="90", cloudHighWaterSeq="120"; no real content/account.
fixtures.action: Desktop saves the SavedItem. On phone, the user opens its detail and taps Copy; while offline, edits its content into a draft based on revision "1" and favorites it in the Collection, creating a separate collection_entry entity id=f4cb7782-2a5c-43e4-a194-0b2d17a30003 at its own initial revision "1" and a separate outbox operation. On explicit foreground resume, shared sync reconciles both operations. Web and desktop reload the SavedItem and relation.
fixtures.assertions: Copy success means only that the user-triggered system clipboard write succeeded; it does not claim paste into another app. Offline query finds the cached item and reports partial coverage ("90" < "120"), never full-cloud coverage. Foreground sync uses the shared T21 engine and commits the content edit once under SavedItem identity 8f14e45f-ea62-4f9f-8c4e-55c8aabb0001, advancing only its content revision from Decimal "1" to "2". Favorite is a distinct collection_entry identity f4cb7782-2a5c-43e4-a194-0b2d17a30003 targeting that SavedItem in Collection 3c15e2ab-f3c6-4a90-9c72-67e1a0e90002, with its own Decimal revision "1"; it does not change the SavedItem content revision or add a pin field. Web and desktop each observe exactly one SavedItem with the same identity/content revision and one relation with the same independent identity/revision; no duplicate or stale overwrite. Each draft/outbox operation clears only with its corresponding committed state. Static fixture literals are not behavior or random-source acceptance.

acceptanceGates.scope: Enumerated dependency frontier: 12 named prerequisite tasks, including T20/T22 upstream links; full recursive dependency closure remains OPEN_QUESTION (T24-OQ01).
Reuse accepted T21 shared TS engine and mobile adapter boundary; no duplicate sync/conflict rules.
Foreground recovery, offline unlocked use, interruption, and no background-sync promise.
Immutable outbox, exact retry/receipt, SENDING→READY, ACK/draft transaction.
Attachment WAIT_DEPENDENCY, pull/cursor/watermark, snapshot/catch-up and cancel reconciliation.
Lock/revoke/account isolation, partial index coverage, no full-cloud claim.
iOS/Android permission and process lifecycle, separately labeled.
Injected capacity, storage, HTTP errors and cancellation data-retention behavior.
Desktop/Web/mobile shared DTO fixture parity and Decimal representation; no crypto-vector substitution.
Independent T04 critical review after planning; no acceptance until issues close.

Physical iOS device: complete the T24-F37 bidirectional user flow—desktop SavedItem reaches phone; user Copy and offline edit plus separate favorite relation sync back; Web and desktop observe matching SavedItem and collection_entry identities/revisions without duplicate or overwrite. Archive platform-specific actual results at docs/evidence/T24/ios-f37-device-lifecycle.json.

Physical Android device: complete the T24-F37 bidirectional user flow—desktop SavedItem reaches phone; user Copy and offline edit plus separate favorite relation sync back; Web and desktop observe matching SavedItem and collection_entry identities/revisions without duplicate or overwrite. Archive platform-specific actual results at docs/evidence/T24/android-f37-device-lifecycle.json.

openQuestions.title: recursive-dependency-closure
openQuestions.question: The listed gate includes T24 direct T21/T23, 03 §11 T24 upstream T16/T18/T19, named T21/T23 upstreams, and inspected T20/T22 links T06/T15 and T06/T07. Deeper recursive task-manifest closure beyond these enumerated edges has not been established; reconcile it and keep T24 gated until all required tasks are accepted.

openQuestions.title: shared-engine-adapter
openQuestions.question: Accepted T21 TypeScript engine exports, mobile repository adapter API, and transaction boundary are not frozen; T24 must reuse shared rules, not fork sync/conflict logic.

openQuestions.title: foreground-background-scheduler
openQuestions.question: Foreground recovery is required; OS background wakeups are best effort. Exact iOS/Android APIs, cadence, cancellation, and presentation are not established.

openQuestions.title: mobile-repository-transactions
openQuestions.question: The precise accepted T22/T23 storage adapter and mapping of shared engine transactions to mobile persistence remain gated.

openQuestions.title: error-and-native-mapping
openQuestions.question: Protocol codes/actions are frozen where specified, but mobile UI copy, native error codes, and retry presentation are not established.

openQuestions.title: attachment-provider-resume
openQuestions.question: WAIT_DEPENDENCY and ATTACHMENT_NOT_READY are frozen; provider behavior, upload resumption, and T18 readiness remain unaccepted.

openQuestions.title: snapshot-recovery-cancel
openQuestions.question: T19 snapshot/lease implementation remains unaccepted; expiry/cancellation mapping and recovery-namespace capacity remain planning-only.

openQuestions.title: offline-index-coverage
openQuestions.question: Shared QueryPage coverage fields exist, but mobile progress UI, index cadence, and interrupted-index recovery require accepted T21 interfaces.

openQuestions.title: mobile-capacity-accounting
openQuestions.question: Configured limits are planning defaults pending benchmark validation. Mobile byte charging, aggregation, storage failure codes, and presentation remain OPEN_QUESTION; fixtures use injected counters only.

openQuestions.title: permission-fallback
openQuestions.question: iOS/Android permission outcomes are symbolic. Exact OS permission names, native codes, and fallback ownership remain with T23/platform acceptance.

openQuestions.title: ambiguous-cancel-result
openQuestions.question: Cancel/timeout cannot prove that the server did not commit. Keep original opId/wire bytes and reconcile operation receipt before a new operation; exact UX remains OPEN_QUESTION.

openQuestions.title: shared-fixture-ownership
openQuestions.question: Authoritative shared fixture path, generator, and owners are not confirmed. T24 records parity assertions only and writes no fixtures/** files.

openQuestions.title: crypto-vector-ownership
openQuestions.question: No crypto outputs or official cross-platform vectors are produced here; vector/KAT acceptance remains owned by T15.

limitations: Fixture planning only. All 37 fixtures, 12 acceptance gates, and 2 commands are NOT_RUN; T24 remains not_started.
T21 and T23 are not accepted; T16/T18/T19 required by 03 §11 and the complete T21/T23 upstream closure remain unaccepted.
The T24 card and 03 §11 dependency sets differ. The plan keeps their union plus the upstream closure of T21 and T23 gated.
No production code, shared fixture, mobile app file, progress block, service, database, provider, native package, device, or user data was touched.
No crypto behavior, encryption output, official cross-platform vector, or parity PASS is claimed; official vectors remain T15-owned.
Mobile storage accounting, OS permission mapping, background scheduler, user-facing error mapping, provider attachment behavior, and snapshot implementation remain OPEN_QUESTION where referenced.
Independent T04 critical review is pending; static evidence does not establish acceptance.
